en: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-'Anazi narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from 'Uthman ibn Ghiyath, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: While the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) was in one of the gardens of Medina, leaning back and poking with a stick he had between the water and the mud, a man asked for the gate to be opened. He said: "Open it and give him the glad tidings of Paradise." He said: It was Abu Bakr, so I opened it for him and gave him the glad tidings of Paradise. He said: Then another man asked for the gate to be opened, so he said: "Open it and give him the glad tidings of Paradise." He said: I went, and behold, it was 'Umar, so I opened it for him and gave him the glad tidings of Paradise. Then another man asked for the gate to be opened—he said—so the Prophet (pbuh) sat up and said: "Open it and give him the glad tidings of Paradise upon an affliction that will befall him." He said: I went, and behold, it was 'Uthman ibn 'Affan. He said: So I opened it and gave him the glad tidings of Paradise. He said: And I told him what he had said, so he said: "O Allah, grant patience!"—or: "Allah is the One whose help is sought."

Amr al-Naqid, al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani, and 'Abd ibn Humayd all narrated it to us from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, my father narrated to us, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from Ibn Shihab, he said: Yahya ibn Sa'id ibn al-'As informed me that Sa'id ibn al-'As informed him that 'Uthman and 'A'ishah both narrated to him that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq asked permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah (pbuh)... and he mentioned the like of the hadith of 'Uqayl from al-Zuhri.

Abd al-Malik ibn Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from my grandfather, 'Uqayl ibn Khalid narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Yahya ibn Sa'id ibn al-'As, that Sa'id ibn al-'As informed him that 'A'ishah, wife of the Prophet (pbuh), and 'Uthman both narrated to him that Abu Bakr asked permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) while he was lying down on his bed, wearing 'A'ishah's woolen blanket. He gave Abu Bakr permission while in that state, so he settled his need with him and then departed. Then 'Umar asked permission, and he gave him permission while in that state, so he settled his need with him and then departed. 'Uthman said: Then I asked permission to enter upon him, so he sat up and said to 'A'ishah: "Gather your garments around you." So I settled my need with him and then departed. 'A'ishah said: "O Messenger of Allah, why is it that I did not see you perturbed for Abu Bakr and 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them) as you were perturbed for 'Uthman?" The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "Indeed, 'Uthman is a very modest man, and I feared that if I gave him permission while in that state, he would not convey his need to me."

Yahya ibn Yahya, Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us—Yahya ibn Yahya said: informed us, and the others said: narrated to us—Isma'il—meaning Ibn Ja'far—from Muhammad ibn Abi Harmalah, from 'Ata' and Sulayman, sons of Yasar, and Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, that 'A'ishah said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) was lying down in my house, with his thighs or his shins uncovered. Abu Bakr asked permission to enter, and he permitted him while in that state, and he conversed. Then 'Umar asked permission, and he permitted him while in that state, and he conversed. Then 'Uthman asked permission, so the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) sat up and straightened his clothes—Muhammad said: and I do not say that this occurred on a single day—and he entered and conversed. When he left, 'A'ishah said: "Abu Bakr entered and you did not stir for him nor pay much heed, then 'Umar entered and you did not stir for him nor pay much heed, then 'Uthman entered and you sat up and straightened your clothes?" He said: "Shall I not feel modest before a man of whom the angels feel modest?"

And Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and 'Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id both narrated it to us—they said: Yahya—and he is al-Qattan—narrated to us, from 'Ubaydullah, with this chain of narration, with the meaning of the hadith of Abu Usamah, and he added: He said: "So he abandoned praying over them."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, 'Ubaydullah narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: When 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul died, his son 'Abdullah ibn 'Abdullah came to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) and asked him to give him his shirt so that he might shroud his father in it, and he gave it to him. Then he asked him to pray the funeral prayer over him, so the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) stood up to pray over him. 'Umar stood up and took hold of the garment of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh), saying: "O Messenger of Allah, will you pray over him when Allah has forbidden you to pray over him?" The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "Allah has only given me the choice, saying: 'Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times...' and I shall add to more than seventy." 'Umar said: "He is a hypocrite!" Yet the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) prayed over him, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "And never pray over any of them who died, nor stand at his grave."

Uqbah ibn Mukram al-'Ammi narrated to us, Sa'id ibn 'Amir narrated to us, he said: Juwayriyah ibn Asma' informed us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: 'Umar said: "I concurred with my Lord in three things: regarding the Station of Ibrahim, regarding the hijab, and regarding the prisoners of Badr."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Layth narrated to us; (H) and 'Amr al-Naqid and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us—they said: Ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us—both of them from Ibn 'Ajlan, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, with this chain of narration, the like of it.

Abu al-Tahir Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn Sarh narrated to me, 'Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, from his father Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Salamah, from 'A'ishah, from the Prophet (pbuh), that he used to say: "Among the nations before you there were people who were inspired; if there is anyone among my nation from them, then 'Umar ibn al-Khattab is among them." Ibn Wahb said: The explanation of muhaddathun is mulhamun (those inspired).

Harun ibn Ma'ruf narrated it to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad narrated it to us, Suhayl informed me, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab came to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) while there were women with him who had raised their voices over the Messenger of Allah (pbuh). When 'Umar asked permission to enter, they rushed to the veil... and he mentioned the like of the hadith of al-Zuhri.

Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim narrated to us, Ibrahim—meaning Ibn Sa'd—narrated to us; (H) and Hasan al-Hulwani and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us—'Abd said: informed me, and Hasan said: Ya'qub—and he is Ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd—narrated to us—my father narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, 'Abd al-Hamid ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd informed me that Muhammad ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas informed him that his father Sa'd said: 'Umar asked permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) while there were women from Quraysh with him speaking to him and asking him for more, their voices raised high. When 'Umar asked permission to enter, they stood up and rushed to veil themselves. The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) gave him permission while the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) was laughing. 'Umar said: "May Allah keep your teeth laughing, O Messenger of Allah!" The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "I marvel at these women who were with me; when they heard your voice, they rushed to veil themselves." 'Umar said: "You, O Messenger of Allah, have more right that they should be in awe of you." Then 'Umar said: "O enemies of yourselves, do you fear me and not fear the Messenger of Allah (pbuh)?" They said: "Yes, you are harsher and sterner than the Messenger of Allah (pbuh)." The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "By the One in Whose hand is my soul, Satan never meets you traversing a path except that he traverses a path other than your path."

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Yunus informed me, that Ibn Shihab informed him, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (pbuh), that he said: "While I was asleep, I saw myself in Paradise, and behold, there was a woman performing ablution beside a palace. I said: 'Whose is this?' They said: ''Umar ibn al-Khattab's.' So I remembered the protective jealousy of 'Umar, and turned back to leave." Abu Hurayrah said: So 'Umar wept while we were all in that gathering with the Messenger of Allah (pbuh), and then 'Umar said: "May my father be ransomed for you, O Messenger of Allah! Would I feel protective jealousy against you?" And 'Amr al-Naqid, Hasan al-Hulwani, and 'Abd ibn Humayd all narrated it to me—they said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, with this chain of narration, the like of it.

And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated it to us, Sufyan informed us, from 'Amr and Ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir; (H) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr, who heard Jabir; (H) and 'Amr al-Naqid narrated it to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn al-Munkadir: I heard Jabir, from the Prophet (pbuh), with the like of the hadith of Ibn Numayr and Zuhayr.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr and Ibn al-Munkadir, who both heard Jabir reporting from the Prophet (pbuh); (H) and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us—and the wording is his—Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ibn al-Munkadir and 'Amr, from Jabir, from the Prophet (pbuh), who said: "I entered Paradise and saw therein a house or a palace. I said: 'Whose is this?' They said: ''Umar ibn al-Khattab's.' So I wished to enter, but remembered your protective jealousy." Thereupon 'Umar wept and said: "O Messenger of Allah, would protective jealousy be felt against you?"

Ahmad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Yunus narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Musa ibn 'Uqbah narrated to me, from Salim ibn 'Abdullah, from his father, concerning the dream of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) regarding Abu Bakr and 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with them both), similar to their hadith.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us—and the wording is Abu Bakr's—they said: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Salim narrated to me, from Salim ibn 'Abdullah, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "I was shown in a dream as if I were drawing water with a bucket using a pulley over a well. Then Abu Bakr came and drew one or two buckets, and drew with a weak draw—and may Allah, Blessed and Exalted, forgive him. Then 'Umar came and drew water, and it turned into a massive bucket; and I have never seen a leader among men work with such tremendous strength as he worked, until the people were fully quenched and settled at the resting places of the camels."

Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb narrated to me, my paternal uncle 'Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, that Abu Yunus, freed slave of Abu Hurayrah, narrated to him from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (pbuh), who said: "While I was asleep, I was shown as if I were drawing water at my cistern, giving the people to drink. Then Abu Bakr came to me and took the bucket from my hand to relieve me, and drew two buckets, and in his drawing was weakness—and may Allah forgive him. Then Ibn al-Khattab came and took it from him, and I have never seen any man's drawing stronger than his, until the people turned away while the cistern was full and bursting with water."

Al-Hulwani and 'Abd ibn Humayd both narrated to us—they said: Ya'qub narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Salih, who said: Al-A'raj and others said that Abu Hurayrah said that the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "I saw the son of Abu Quhafah drawing water..." similar to the hadith of al-Zuhri.

And 'Abd al-Malik ibn Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to me, my father narrated to me, from my grandfather, 'Uqayl ibn Khalid narrated to me; (H) and 'Amr al-Naqid, al-Hulwani, and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, my father narrated to us, from Salih, with the chain of narration of Yunus, similar to his hadith.

Harmalah narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, that Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab informed him that he heard Abu Hurayrah saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) saying: "While I was asleep, I saw myself at a well upon which was a bucket, and I drew from it whatever Allah willed. Then the son of Abu Quhafah took it and drew with it one or two buckets, and in his drawing—and may Allah forgive him—was weakness. Then it turned into a huge bucket, and the son of al-Khattab took it, and I have never seen a leader among men draw with such drawing as 'Umar ibn al-Khattab drew, until the people settled their camels at the watering place."

And Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated it to us, Layth narrated to us, from 'Uqayl; (H) and al-Hulwani and 'Abd ibn Humayd both narrated to us from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, my father narrated to us, from Salih, with the chain of narration of Yunus, similar to his hadith.

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Yunus informed me, that Ibn Shihab informed him, from Hamzah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah (pbuh), who said: "While I was asleep, I saw a cup of milk brought to me, and I drank from it until I could see the freshness flowing out of my fingernails. Then I gave my leftover to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab." They said: "How did you interpret that, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Knowledge."

Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Salih ibn Kaysan; (H) and Zuhayr ibn Harb, al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani, and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us—and the wording is theirs—they said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, Abu Umamah ibn Sahl narrated to me that he heard Abu Sa'id al-Khudri saying: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "While I was asleep, I saw people presented before me wearing shirts: some reached the breasts and some reached below that. And 'Umar ibn al-Khattab passed by wearing a shirt that he was dragging." They said: "How did you interpret that, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The religion."
And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, 'Isa ibn Yunus informed us, from 'Umar ibn Sa'id, in this chain of narration, the like of it.

Sa'id ibn 'Amr al-Ash'athi, Abu al-Rabi' al-'Ataki, and Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us—and the wording is Abu Kurayb's—Abu al-Rabi' said: narrated to us, and the other two said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from 'Umar ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Husayn, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: I heard Ibn 'Abbas saying: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab was placed upon his bier, and the people surrounded him, supplicating, praising, and praying over him before he was lifted, and I was among them. He said: Nothing startled me except a man who took hold of my shoulder from behind me. I turned to him, and behold, it was 'Ali! He invoked mercy upon 'Umar and said: "You have not left behind anyone more beloved to me to meet Allah with deeds like his than you. And by Allah, I truly thought that Allah would place you with your two companions! That is because I often used to hear the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) saying: 'I, Abu Bakr, and 'Umar came; I, Abu Bakr, and 'Umar entered; I, Abu Bakr, and 'Umar went out.' So I used to hope, or think, that Allah would place you with the two of them."

And Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated it to us—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn 'Abbad narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Mis'ar—both of them from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (pbuh).

And Muhammad ibn 'Abbad narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me, Abu Dawud al-Hafari narrated to us, from Sufyan—both of them from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (pbuh), with the meaning of the hadith of Yunus from al-Zuhri. And in both their hadiths is mention of the cow and the sheep together, and they both said in their hadith: "'For indeed I believe in it, I, Abu Bakr, and 'Umar,' while they were not there."

And 'Abd al-Malik ibn Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to me, my father narrated to me, from my grandfather, 'Uqayl ibn Khalid narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, with this chain of narration: the story of the sheep and the wolf, and he did not mention the story of the cow.

Abu al-Tahir Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn Sarh and Harmalah ibn Yahya both narrated to me—they said: Ibn Wahb informed us, Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to me that they heard Abu Hurayrah saying: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "While a man was driving a cow of his upon which he had placed a burden, the cow turned to him and said: 'Indeed, I was not created for this; rather, I was created only for plowing.'" The people said in astonishment and alarm: "Subhan Allah! A cow talks?!" The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "Indeed, I believe in it, I, Abu Bakr, and 'Umar." Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "While a shepherd was among his sheep, a wolf attacked them and took a sheep from them. The shepherd pursued it until he rescued it from him. The wolf turned to him and said: 'Who will protect it on the Day of Beasts, a day when it will have no shepherd other than me?'" The people said: "Subhan Allah!" The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "Indeed, I believe in that, I, Abu Bakr, and 'Umar."

Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd informed us, Salih ibn Kaysan narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said to me during his illness: "Call Abu Bakr and your brother for me so that I may write a document, for I fear that an aspirant will wish and a speaker will say, 'I am more worthy,' whereas Allah and the believers refuse anyone except Abu Bakr."
